components.gap: The source's Remark after Theorem 2.1.7 (Durrett p. 47) is not supplied: for the factorization class L = {A : P(A cap F) = P(A)P(F)} it is not easy to show closure under intersections or unions, whereas closure under proper differences B - A (A subset of B) is easy to check, which is why the proof runs through a lambda-system and the pi-lambda theorem. Annex 115-139 verifies the lambda-system properties but states neither half of this justification.

source_locators.content: necessity chain, remarks on expectations and fair games, Theorem 2

components.gap: Feller, Volume II, VII.7 (pp. 234-237), which this boundary routes to the Feller chapters, is not fully supplied on the route. The mathematics is present (thm:p15-feller-truncation-inequality, thm:p15-feller-generalized-weak-law, thm:p15-feller-centering-corollaries, thm:p15-feller-positive-weak-normalization), but these source claims are absent: (i) the historical claim that the oldest version of the law of large numbers is the finite-variance identically distributed form (7.1), which is contained in Chebyshev's inequality (p. 234); (ii) the attribution of the finite-expectation weak law to Khintchine (Khintchine's law of large numbers, p. 235); (iii) the remark that inequality (7.4) is valid also for dependent variables with varying distributions (p. 235); (iv) the remark (p. 236) that even when expectations exist a participant in a fair game may be strongly on the losing side.
